beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Sawadee, this is Liam, in for Bear. Today we tear down a skill that answers a question every fellow keeps hitting: how long should this video be? The honest answer is you don't decide. The content decides. The skill is called duration-planner, and here is how it actually works.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer corrects the reel's actual misconception ('target') into its claim ('output'). Trigger uses SINGLE TOKENS per BrutalistHesitantWriter contract; multi-word phrases silently never match.
beats.narration_text: The easy assumption is that duration is a target you hit — thirty seconds, one minute, five. The skill argues the opposite. Duration is an output. You size the script and let the content sit for the time it needs to land. Everything else is production convenience or padding.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — duration is an output. The thesis.
beats.narration_text: First design decision, and it's the thesis. Quote from the SKILL file: duration is an output, never a target. A complex mechanism lands at three or four minutes. A definitional explainer at thirty to sixty seconds. Both are correct. A uniform target has no learning basis — it's a production convenience that either compresses the content and destroys integration, or pads it and adds extraneous load. Either way, learning fails.

props.heading: Duration is an output.
props.body: A complex mechanism lands at 3–4 minutes. A definitional explainer at 30–60 seconds. BOTH are correct. A uniform target compresses the content OR pads it — either extraneous load, either learning failure.
props.quote: Duration is an OUTPUT, never a target.

beats.role_note: Worked example / Design decision 2 — the consolidation floor and the content_type table.
beats.narration_text: Second decision. Every beat has a content_type, and each content_type has a consolidation floor — the minimum time working memory needs to register the new element before the beat cuts. A title beat needs three to five seconds. A structure or geometric beat, six to eight. A mechanism step, six to ten. An equation step, seven to twelve. If your narration lands under the floor, don't shorten the next beat and don't speed up the voice. Add a hold.

show.event: eyebrow MECHANISM · ACT 2 lands
heading 'The consolidation floor.' lands
body: the content_type floors reveal one row at a time
quote block: 'Floors are minimums, enforced with holds.'
verdict pill 'floor ≠ padding — it's the load-bearing rule'

props.heading: The consolidation floor.
props.body: title → 3–5s  ·  realworld → 4–5s  ·  structure → 6–8s  ·  data → 6–8s  ·  mechanism → 6–10s  ·  equation → 7–12s. Below the floor → HOLD. Over the ceiling → SPLIT.
props.quote: Floors are minimums, enforced with holds.

beats.role_note: Design tell / falsifiability — padding is a coherence violation, and engagement is not the target.
beats.narration_text: Here is where the skill bites. Once the idea has landed, adding decorative motion or filler graphics to reach one minute is a coherence violation — extraneous load that degrades learning. Padding to hit thirty seconds is exactly as wrong as compressing to hit it. And the six-minute engagement rule everyone quotes? That's a watch-time finding from open MOOCs. It doesn't replicate in real courses, and it isn't a learning result. The trade the skill accepts: shorter watchtime, cleaner schema.

show.event: eyebrow DESIGN · TELL lands
heading 'Padding is a coherence violation.' lands
body: extraneous load, six-minute rule debunk
quote: 'Padding to reach 1:00 is as wrong as compressing to reach 0:30.'
verdict pill 'trades watchtime for schema' (negative pill — the real cost)

props.heading: Padding is a coherence violation.
props.body: Motion after the idea has landed is extraneous load — not a style, a defect. The six-minute engagement rule is a MOOC watchtime finding; it does not replicate in enrolled courses and it is not a learning result.
props.quote: Padding to reach 1:00 is as wrong as compressing to reach 0:30.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates the beat.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. The duration-planner skill is small on disk and long on discipline. Content_type drives the floor. Kokoro drives the clock. Holds land the beats. Splits break up over-full ones. Total runtime is a byproduct — the skill reports it and stops. And it refuses to pad or compress to hit a number production wanted for its own convenience.

show.event: artifact card scales in, filling frame
heading 'The duration-planner verdict.' lands
five verdict lines reveal one at a time

artifactLines: Duration is an output — the content decides the clock, never a fixed 30s or 1min target.
content_type on every beat sets the consolidation floor working memory needs.
Kokoro narration is the master clock; assemble.py pads audio to match the video hold.
Below-floor beats get a hold; over-ceiling beats split into two ideas, never one long one.
Total runtime is a byproduct — the skill reports it and stops. pace_check.py never edits.
Refuses to pad or compress to hit a target: coherence violation, not a style choice.
